clinical.citation: Stephenson et al. 2017 - A Novel Human CAMK2A Mutation Disrupts Dendritic Morphology and Synaptic Transmission, and Causes ASD-Related Behaviors (PMID: 28130356)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo variant in a proband with ASD; functional studies showed reduced substrate phosphorylation and autophosphorylation, dominant-negative effect, and altered dendritic and synaptic phenotypes; knock-in mice show ASD-related behaviors

clinical.citation: Deletion of a Single Lysine Residue at Position 292 of CAMK2A Disrupts Protein Function, Causing Severe Epileptic Encephalopathy and Intellectual Disability (PMID: 37510258)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo heterozygous in-frame deletion identified by exome sequencing; affects a crucial functional site and is predicted to alter protein structure and function; phenotype consistent with IDD autosomal dominant 53

clinical.citation: Genetic Traces in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Whole Exome Sequencing Study from Türkiye (PMID: 41751633)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: classified likely pathogenic (PM2, PS2, PP2, PP3, PP5); de novo; associated with intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 53

clinical.citation: Diagnostic Yield of Whole Exome Sequencing in Autism Spectrum Disorder Patients at a Tertiary Center in Saudi Arabia (PMID: 42606785)

variants.description: not specified; CAMK2A listed among recurrently affected genes

clinical.diagnostic_reason: variants classified per ACMG/AMP guidelines on clinical WES; per-patient details not given in the abstract

clinical.citation: ASHG 2023 - Deciphering the genetic architecture of autism spectrum disorder using chromosomal microarray and whole exome sequencing in patient-parent trios in India

variants.description: de novo SNV in CAMK2A (specific variant not given)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo SNV in a known ASD gene identified by trio WES

model_organism.citation: Adult Camk2a gene reinstatement restores the learning and plasticity deficits of Camk2a knockout mice (PMID: 36304100)
phenotypes: Camk2a knockout mice show deficits in spatial learning, conditional learning and synaptic plasticity
Inducible Camk2a model: adult re-expression of CAMK2A rescued the behavioral and electrophysiological deficits
CAMK2A does not appear to play a critical irreversible developmental role

model_organism.citation: Involvement of Ca(2+)-Dependent Hyperpolarization in Sleep Duration in Mammals (PMID: 26996081)
phenotypes: Camk2a KO mice showed decreased sleep duration
Camk2b KO mice showed the same decrease
Part of a screen of 21 KO mouse lines supporting a Ca(2+)-dependent hyperpolarization pathway in sleep regulation
model_organism.sample_size: 21 KO lines screened overall; per-line n not given in abstract

model_organism.citation: NMDA receptors on zebrafish Mauthner cells require CaMKII-α for normal development (PMID: 25047640)
phenotypes: Morpholino knockdown of CaMKII-α did not significantly change AMPA mEPSCs
NMDA mEPSC amplitude decreased, specifically the slow component (τslow ≈ 300 ms); fast component, frequency and kinetics were unaffected
Increased dendritic arborization of Mauthner cells in morphants
camk2a was the only CaMKII gene with detectable mRNA in M-cells at 2 dpf

biological.citation: Kury et al. 2017 - De Novo Mutations in Protein Kinase Genes CAMK2A and CAMK2B Cause Intellectual Disability (PMID: 29100089)
biological.summary: De novo CAMK2A/CAMK2B variants from 24 individuals with ID were found to either decrease or increase CAMK2 Thr286/287 autophosphorylation. All variants affecting autophosphorylation also impaired neuronal migration, showing that tightly regulated autophosphorylation is needed for neurodevelopment. CAMK2 is placed in the glutamatergic (AMPAR/NMDAR) signaling pathway.

biological.citation: Mouse knock-in study 2025 - A hyper-activatable CAMK2A variant associated with intellectual disability causes exaggerated long-term potentiation and learning impairments (PMID: 40140673)
biological.summary: Heterozygous P212L Camk2a knock-in mice showed increased CaMKIIα autophosphorylation (gain of function), dendritic spine abnormalities, exaggerated hippocampal LTP after subthreshold low-frequency stimulation, and learning/behavioral deficits that resemble human ID/NDD.

biological.citation: Temporal and region-specific requirements of αCaMKII in spatial and contextual learning (PMID: 25143599)
biological.summary: Conditional Camk2a deletion in mice showed that forebrain deletion, but not cerebellar deletion, severely impairs water maze and contextual fear learning. Adult-onset deletion was as damaging as germline deletion for learning and synaptic plasticity, so αCaMKII must be intact at the time of learning.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - De novo variants affecting autoinhibition of Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II, cause neurodevelopmental disorders
biological.summary: CAMK2A missense variants are predicted to disrupt kinase-regulatory segment autoinhibition. A splice variant causes exon 11 skipping in a minigene assay, and Thr286 phosphorylation is increased in Neuro-2a cells. CaMKIIα P212Q expression in primary hippocampal neurons increased A-type K+ currents and facilitated spike repolarization.
biological.significance: reported as significant for A-type K+ current increase

biological.citation: Shah et al. ASHG 2023 - Deciphering the genetic architecture of autism spectrum disorder using chromosomal microarray and whole exome sequencing in patient-parent trios in India
biological.summary: A de novo CAMK2A SNV was found among known ASD genes in an Indian ASD trio cohort, which supports CAMK2A as an ASD/NDD gene involved in synaptic function.

biological.citation: circADAMTS6 via stabilizing CAMK2A is involved in smoking-induced emphysema through driving M2 macrophage polarization (PMID: 38936066)
biological.summary: In macrophages, circADAMTS6 stabilizes CAMK2A mRNA by forming a circADAMTS6/IGF2BP2/CAMK2A RNA-protein ternary complex. This activates CREB and drives M2 polarization and emphysema after cigarette smoke exposure.

biological.citation: Targeting the exosomal CaMK2A-ZDHHC3-GPX4 pathway reprograms tumor-associated macrophages and enhances anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy in gastric cancer (PMID: 42328444)
biological.summary: Gastric cancer-derived exosomal CaMK2A phosphorylates ZDHHC3 at Thr176, which increases GPX4 S-palmitoylation at Cys10 and stabilizes GPX4. This suppresses macrophage ferroptosis and promotes M2 TAM polarization.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-3200-3p targeting CAMK2A modulates the proliferation and metastasis of glioma in vitro (PMID: 35287547)
biological.summary: CAMK2A is a direct target of miR-3200-3p in glioma cells. CAMK2A overexpression reversed the anti-proliferative and anti-metastatic effects of the miRNA, and CAMK2A acts through the Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK pathway.

biological.citation: Plasma CAMK2A predicts chemotherapy resistance in metastatic triple negative breast cancer (PMID: 31938151)
biological.summary: Plasma CAMK2A was higher in chemotherapy-resistant metastatic TNBC patients (ELISA validation). High levels predicted shorter overall survival (13.9 vs 28.9 months).

biological.citation: Camk2a suppresses denervated muscle atrophy by maintaining the Ca2+ homeostasis in muscle cells (PMID: 38015546)
biological.summary: Camk2a expression fell in denervated muscle as Ca2+ rose. Camk2a overexpression reduced Ca2+ accumulation, preserved muscle mass and fiber cross-sectional area, and reduced collagen deposition, so Camk2a helps maintain Ca2+ homeostasis in muscle.

biological.citation: Camk2a-Cre and Tshz3 Expression in Mouse Striatal Cholinergic Interneurons: Implications for Autism Spectrum Disorder (PMID: 34349780)
biological.summary: Lineage tracing showed the Camk2a-Cre transgene is active in striatal cholinergic interneurons as well as projection neurons. Camk2a is therefore expressed in striatal interneurons, which complicates interpretation of Camk2a-Cre conditional knockouts.
